thread:
matt_prod: heads-up — customer-facing 429 surge starting ~12:05 UTC, lots of requests hitting rategate-v4 after the midnight rollout. seeing sustained >10% 429s for some high-volume tenants :alarm_clock:

lucy_sre: oncall-pager triggered. looking at dashboard now — total token acceptance rate dropped, error rate spike from exemptions path. linking graphs: https://grafana/redwood/d/something/rategate-v4

oncall-bot: Paging @lucy_sre (on-call) for incidents: high 429 rate affecting multiple tenants. Incident priority: P1.

lucy_sre: copying in ana_cs + jenna_eng. ana — can you confirm customer impact from CS side? any live tickets?

ana_cs: ana_cs here — we already have 3 escalations from two mid-market customers complaining their API calls are being throttled even for exempt endpoints. They reported degraded user flows and error spikes in the last 10–15m.

jenna_eng: I rolled rategate-v4 through canary at 00:40 UTC. Canary metrics looked ok on low qps but we didn't hit the high-exemptions path during canary traffic (our replay missed that tenant signature).

matt_prod: symptoms match missing exemptions during rollout — looks like exemption lists didn't propagate to some routing nodes, causing tokens that should be exempt to be treated as normal and get rate-limited.

lucy_sre: find root quickly. First mitigation: disable rategate-v4 feature flag to fall back to v3. If that doesn't reduce customer 429s within 2 min, do rollback. Jenna — can you flip flag? I’ll start mitigation runbook.

jenna_eng: flipping flag now — /api/flags/flip {"flag":"rategate_v4_enabled","value":false} 

jenna_eng: (after) flag flip acknowledged by deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: Feature flag rategate_v4_enabled set to false by jenna_eng at 12:11:06 UTC.

lucy_sre: monitoring metrics... traffic acceptance increasing, 429s dropping on aggregate but still seeing handful of regions with elevated 429s (possible cache carryover or slow node config).

ops_tom: if some nodes missed the flag sync, we should also force a config push. running config-sync to all routing nodes now:
```
for node in $(list-nodes --role=rategate); do scp config.json $node:/etc/rategate/config.json && ssh $node systemctl restart rategate; done
```

ops_tom: pushed and restarted.

lucy_sre: good — checking per-tenant rates. Numbers look much better. Customer error reports reducing. Ana, can you confirm the CS queue?

ana_cs: verifying with customers — two of three confirm normal behaviour returned. I'll keep monitoring and follow up with any lingering reports.

matt_prod: root cause hypothesis: rollout process wrote exemption table to the new store but a race in the deploy job meant some routing nodes switched to the new binary before store replication finished. v4 treated missing entries as deny-by-default leading to over-throttle. This is a bad interplay of deploy order + eventual consistency.

jenna_eng: agreed. we need a hotfix: ensure deploy job waits for exemption-store sync, and add deploy-time verification to sample exempted tokens across nodes. I'll open a short-lived PR and patch the deploy pipeline.

lucy_sre: for now, leave flag off and keep throttles at v3. Jenna — file a rollback postmortem and link action items. Matt — please send an incident severity notice to ops and product. I'll mark this P1 and start the incident timeline.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-01. Severity P1. Channel: #incidents. Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/rategate_release_issues

jenna_eng: quick checklist items I’m doing now:
- PR for deploy wait + verification (jenna/rg-v4-fix)
- integration test to replay exemption-heavy tenant traffic in canary
- add monitoring alert for exemption propagation latency

matt_prod: escalation note for customer comms: affected tenants saw increased 429s for ~8–12 minutes depending on region. We should offer credits for impacted windows and summarize what went wrong.

ana_cs: noted — drafting customer-facing timeline and apology. will coordinate with sales for any compensation.

lucy_sre: handoff to next oncall in 30 min — @ops_tom will monitor for 1 hour and then we’ll transition to post-incident review. Any objections?

ops_tom: ack — I'll watch the dashboard and the exemption-store replication metrics (replication_lag_seconds). Also will run a token-accounting reconciliation job to detect any units miscounted during the event.

jenna_eng: pushed a quick PR and test. Planning to merge after one more review. I won't re-enable rategate-v4 until we have the deploy-order guard and a canary replay with exemption traffic.

lucy_sre: action items (summarized):
- jenna_eng: deploy pipeline change + canary replay test (owner)
- ops_tom: run token-accounting reconciliation + monitor for anomalies (owner)
- ana_cs: customer comms and credits coordination (owner)
- matt_prod: incident summary & severity notice to leadership (owner)

lucy_sre: closing the immediate pager — flag flip + config sync mitigated majority impact. Keeping incident open for follow-up and postmortem. If anything new shows up, reopen thread. :white_check_mark:

ana_cs: thanks team — I'll post an update to affected customers in ~45m unless we see more regressions.

ops_tom: reconciliation job started at 12:28 UTC. will post results here when done.

jenna_eng: merging pipeline guard PR now, will schedule a replay canary for 03:00 UTC to simulate exemption-heavy flows.

lucy_sre: last check — 429s steady at baseline. setting last_message_ts to 1769994600 and tagging for postmortem.

matt_prod: thanks everyone.
